title: An operational perturbation proteomics-based virtual cell model.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Europe PMC has no full text or PMCID (paywalled), and no supplement, accessions or NCBI links. I fetched the JavaScript of the ProteinTalks-DB website (db.prottalks.com). Its download page is a request form: name, institutional email (checked server-side), PI (lab head) name and email, lab URL, a usage statement of at least 20 characters, and a captcha. The link is then emailed, and requests can be forwarded to aivc@westlakeomics.com. The site's licence covers non-commercial academic use only and forbids derivative works. I listed the GitHub repo guomics-lab/PTV-1: R analysis scripts plus ProteinTalks model code under an MIT licence and a 10 MB checkpoint, but no data files. The ProteomeXchange (proteomics data exchange) API search for IPX0007409000 returned 0 datasets, and the iProX proxi query returned HTTP 400.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: From the abstract, press coverage and search snippets: 38 million protein-abundance values, 18 breast cancer cell lines (16 triple-negative), 63 approved drugs and 59 combinations, sampled at 0, 6, 24 and 48 h. Snippets cite 16,311 proteome profiles and 23,554 cell-viability measurements, and say raw mass-spec data are at iProX IPX0007409000. I verified none of these counts.

a1_downloadable.note: Failed, checked on the site. The processed protein matrix is only given out through a request form (institutional email, PI details, usage statement, captcha) with the link sent by email: an access application. The only other copy is raw mass-spec files on iProX, which we don't download, and ProteomeXchange returned no public record.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Not checked: no files obtained. The code reads a pheno.csv of binary efficacy/synergy labels, but whether the released data includes it is unknown.

a5_enough_rows.note: Paper-only claims: 16,311 profiles and 23,554 viability measurements. Not verified.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Not checked. A matrix of about 16k profiles by about 10k proteins would be a few GB as floats, which is plausible on a laptop, but unverified.

a8_label_provenance.note: Not checked. Per the paper, the labels come from measured viability, made binary by the authors.

existing_models.name: ProteinTalks (the paper's own neural ODE, a differential-equation network model)
existing_models.score_and_split: Not retrieved: the full text is paywalled. The repo's default split is a random 70/20/10.

backbone.name: none standard; ProteinTalks checkpoint (MIT code)
backbone.licence: Code MIT; data non-commercial, no derivative works

integration.partner_dataset: DepMap / GDSC drug sensitivity (would be joined on cell line and drug)
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Do drug-induced protein changes over time predict response better than baseline omics in other cell lines?

controls.external_validation: The paper mentions organoids and biopsies; availability unknown.

honest_claim_h3: Not stated: the data could not be obtained without an access request.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use protein levels measured over time after drug treatment to predict whether a drug or drug pair kills breast cancer cells.
plain_idea.train_on: Proteome snapshots at 0, 6, 24 and 48 hours after treatment, plus drug chemical fingerprints, for breast cancer cell lines. Number of examples unknown (the paper claims 16,311 profiles).
plain_idea.predict: Drug efficacy or synergy as a yes/no label, derived by the authors from measured cell viability.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Cancer drug-screening groups could rank drug combinations before running them in the lab. But only if the data can be obtained.

ml_idea: Test whether early (6 h) protein-change signatures predict the final drug response in held-out cell lines or drugs, compared with baseline-only proteomes. Blocked on access to the data.

effort.compute_note: No estimate possible: the data was never obtained.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Submit the db.prottalks.com request and see whether the emailed files include the viability/synergy labels as a table.

verdict_reason: A1 fails, checked on the site. The processed proteomics matrix needs a request form with institutional email, PI details and a usage statement, and the link is emailed. The licence is non-commercial with no derivative works. The only public copy is raw mass-spec data on iProX, which we don't download. Could be reconsidered if the request is granted.
